data.text: WATCH: A fire broke out at a compound along Internal Road in Quezon City on Friday night. | 🎥: Marc Anthony Reyes https://t.co/uecIOgZLU5

🚨 IRAN WAR — DAY 6. Here’s 10 Latest Updates Every Pinoy Should Know…

1.  US Navy submarine torpedoed the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena in the Indian Ocean, just 40 nautical miles off Sri Lanka. Dozens of crew were rescued or recovered — the war has officially jumped out of the Middle East and into waters that affect global shipping routes closer to home.

2.  An Iranian drone struck the UK’s RAF Akrotiri base in Cyprus. Britain is now directly hit, and UK forces are on high alert — this is no longer “someone else’s fight.”

3.  The Strait of Hormuz is under heavy threat — tanker traffic has stalled and insurance costs have skyrocketed. Qatar’s Energy Minister warned prices could hit $150/barrel if it drags on. For the Philippines (which imports ~80% of its oil from the Middle East), this means the biggest fuel-price shock in Asia.

4.  Pump prices in the Philippines are about to explode next week: up to +₱7.09/liter gasoline and +₱15.33/liter diesel expected. DOE already warning gasoline could cross ₱80/liter if the crisis lasts. Jeepney drivers, commuters, and families will feel it first — Marcos is urging everyone to save fuel and carpool.

5.  Over 2 million OFWs in the Gulf are in the danger zone. More than 1,400 have already requested urgent repatriation (especially from UAE, Qatar, and Israel). Hundreds of Pinoys are stranded at closed airports in Dubai, Riyadh, and elsewhere. Marcos has ordered DFA and DMW to prepare full evacuation plans — land routes and chartered buses are being lined up.

6.  Thousands of flights cancelled daily across the Middle East. Philippine Airlines, Cebu Pacific, Emirates, Etihad, Qatar Airways, and others have grounded routes. Pinoys returning home or heading to work are stuck — Clark and NAIA have already helped nearly 1,000 stranded OFWs in the last few days.

7.  Remittances at risk. Saudi, UAE, and Qatar send home over $5 billion a year to Filipino families. Any long shutdown in the Gulf means slower money flows, possible job losses, and tighter household budgets back home.

8.  Iran’s death toll has passed 1,000 (including civilians). Iranian retaliation has hit US bases in Iraq and Gulf cities — the US and Israel say they are “accelerating, not slowing down.” President Trump says 4-5 weeks of combat still ahead. No timeline for when the oil starts flowing again

9.  The Philippines is NOT sending troops and our EDCA bases are NOT being used for this war. Manila has made that crystal clear. But Duterte allies are already warning that US ties could drag us into bigger trouble with China in the West Philippine Sea if America gets stretched too thin.

10.  Inside the Philippines: Business groups are begging the government for fuel subsidies and price controls. Caritas Philippines and economists are calling for rapid shift to renewables so we never get this vulnerable again. President Marcos just held a special Cabinet meeting on energy security.

This is Day 6 — and it is already hitting Filipino wallets, jobs, and families harder than almost anywhere else in Asia.

Stay safe, conserve fuel, check on your OFW relatives, and turn on notifications. This one affects every Pinoy household. 🇵🇭
